# How to Set Up a Shared Grocery List in Alexa That Anyone Can Add to by Voice

> **In short:** You can set up a shared shopping list in Alexa so that any family member, by just speaking to any Echo speaker in the house, can add items instantly — no phone needed, no one forgetting to write it down.

The key piece is **Amazon Household**, a feature that links family accounts so they can see and use the same lists. Once the list is set up, your teenager, roommate, or partner can say "Alexa, add eggs to the shopping list" and it appears for everyone. Here is how to get it running.

## Before you start
- An **Amazon account** and at least one **Echo speaker or Alexa-enabled device** already set up and connected to Wi-Fi.
- The **Alexa app** installed on your phone (available on iPhone and Android — the steps look similar on both).
- Family members you want to share with also need their own Amazon accounts. Amazon Household works with up to two adults and teens/children in the same household.
- About **10 minutes** total for the whole setup, then it works for everyone, forever.

---

## Step 1 — Open the Alexa app and find your lists

Unlock your phone and tap the **Alexa app** icon (a blue rounded triangle on a white background — it may be on your home screen or in your app drawer). If you are not already signed in, the app will ask you to sign in with your Amazon account.

Look along the bottom of the screen for a row of icons. Tap the icon that looks like a **small stack of horizontal lines or a hamburger menu** — this is usually labeled "More" and it opens a side panel. If you do not see it right away, swipe up slightly from the bottom of the screen.

In that side panel, look for a line that says **"Shopping List"** with a small shopping-bag icon next to it. Tap it. This is where your grocery and household shopping lists live.

💬 Example: If your household already has a shared Amazon account, you might find a list called "Shopping List" already there. If you see "My List" or a personal name, that is fine — you will rename it in the next step.

You'll know it worked when you see a screen showing your shopping list, or a prompt to create your first list.

---

## Step 2 — Rename or confirm your shared list

If you already see a shopping list on screen, tap the **list's name** at the top (it might say "Shopping List" or "My List" — tapping it opens a settings screen). If you do not see any list yet, tap the blue **"+" button or "Create List"** button near the top of the screen, then type a name like "Family Grocery List."

On the settings screen that opens, you can edit the list name to something clear that every family member will recognize — something like "Grocery List" or "Weekly Shopping." This name is what everyone will say out loud, so keep it short and simple.

After naming it, look for a toggle or setting labeled **"Shared with Household"** or **"Household List."** This is the setting that makes the list visible and editable to everyone in your Amazon Household. Tap to turn it on. If you do not see this option, it means your Amazon Household may not be set up yet — jump to Step 3 first, then come back.

💬 Example: Name your list "Grocery List" so that anyone in the house can say "add bananas to Grocery List" without confusion.

You'll know it worked when you see a checkmark or the word "Shared" appear next to your list name, or when other household members can see the same list in their Alexa apps.

---

## Step 3 — Set up Amazon Household (if needed)

If Step 2 did not give you a sharing option, your Amazon Household is not configured yet. Open a web browser on your phone or computer and go to **amazon.com/household** (Amazon's Household settings page). Sign in with the Amazon account that owns the Echo device.

On this page, Amazon will walk you through adding adults and teens to your household. Each adult gets their own Amazon account and login — this is how Alexa knows who is in your household. Once family members are linked, they can access your shared lists through their own Alexa apps.

If you are using an older Alexa app, you may also find Household settings by going to **More → Settings → Household Profiles** inside the Alexa app itself. Look for a button labeled **"Add Profile"** or **"Invite Adult."**

💬 Example: Tap "Invite Adult," enter your partner's email address, and they will receive an email to join your Household — it takes about two minutes to complete.

You'll know it worked when the Household page shows two adult profiles, or when family members can open their Alexa apps and see the same shared list you just created.

---

## Step 4 — Verify the list appears in another household member's app

Ask a family member to open the **Alexa app** on their phone. Have them sign in with their own Amazon account (the one you just added to the Household). They do not need to set up their own Echo — just having the app installed is enough.

In their app, go to **More → Shopping List** the same way you did in Step 1. They should see the same list name you created — and if you made changes to it in Step 2, those changes will show up here immediately. This is the proof that the list is truly shared.

If the family member does not see the list, go back to Step 2 and double-check that "Shared with Household" is turned on. Sometimes the setting takes a moment to sync across devices — wait about 30 seconds and refresh.

💬 Example: Your partner opens their app, goes to Shopping List, and sees "Grocery List" right there — with nothing on it yet, or perhaps with whatever you already added.

You'll know it worked when a second person can open their app and see the exact same list name and contents without any extra steps.

---

## Step 5 — Test adding an item by voice from an Echo speaker

Now comes the payoff. Stand near any Echo speaker in your home and say a natural command out loud. Start with:

💬 Example: **"Alexa, add milk to Grocery List."**

After you speak, the Echo speaker's light ring will flash briefly, and Alexa will usually say something back like "Added milk to Grocery List." The item appears on the shared list in your app immediately.

Now pick up the phone from the family member who verified the list in Step 4. Open their Alexa app and check the Shopping List — milk should already be there, without them doing anything. This is the moment the whole system clicks into place.

If Alexa does not respond or says it could not find the list, check that the list name you said matches exactly what you typed in Step 2 — even a small difference like "Groceries List" versus "Grocery List" can cause Alexa to create a new separate list instead.

💬 Example: Say "Alexa, add bread to Grocery List" and then confirm it appears in the app within about five seconds.

You'll know it worked when the item shows up on the shared list in your app (or a family member's app) within a few seconds of speaking the command.

---

## Step 6 — Practice the quick-add voice pattern everyone will use

The magic of this system is that no one in the house needs to touch a phone. Once the list is set up, every household member can add items hands-free. Here are the most useful voice patterns to use:

💬 Example: Say **"Alexa, add chicken breasts to Grocery List"** for a protein item. Or **"Alexa, put laundry detergent on Grocery List"** for a household staple. To remove something someone else added by mistake: **"Alexa, remove milk from Grocery List."**

To see what is on the list without opening your phone, just say **"Alexa, what's on my Grocery List?"** — Alexa will read the items aloud. This is useful while you are at the store with your hands full.

If you are in a noisy room and Alexa mishears you, just repeat the command more clearly. Alexa saves a voice transcript in the app under each list item so you can check exactly what it understood — useful if a strange item mysteriously appears.

💬 Example: Say **"Alexa, add apples to Grocery List"** and then ask **"Alexa, what's on the Grocery List?"** to hear it read back.

You'll know it worked when any household member can stand in the kitchen and add something to the list without picking up a phone — and everyone else sees it appear within seconds.

---

## Common mistakes

- **The list name does not match what you say out loud.** If you created a list called "Weekly Shopping" but say "add eggs to Grocery List," Alexa may create a brand-new separate list called "Grocery List" instead. Say the name exactly as you typed it, or rename the list to something everyone will remember and use consistently.
- **Forgetting to check that family members are signed into the Alexa app, not just logged into the Echo.** The Echo speaker responds to voice, but each person needs the Alexa app on their own phone to see and manage the list from anywhere — even while they are at the store. Make sure everyone downloads the app and signs in, even if they do not own an Echo.
- **Trying to share the list without completing Amazon Household first.** The "Shared with Household" option in Step 2 only appears once Amazon Household is set up. Without that step, the list stays personal to one account even if two people have the app on their phones.

---

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** No more "I forgot to write it down" moments. The moment you realize you are out of butter — whether you are in the kitchen, the garage, or getting dressed — you say it to the nearest Echo and it is on the list. Everyone in the household stays in sync.
- **For your business or work:** If you share a small office with a handful of people, the same shared list setup works for office supplies or shared pantry items. Voice entry means nobody needs to stop what they are doing to open a spreadsheet or app.
- **If you want to go further:** You can create multiple lists for different purposes — one for groceries, one for home improvement items, one for a party — and share each one with specific people. Alexa can also reorder items on your list by priority if you say "move milk to the top of my Grocery List," which is handy when you are working through a long list quickly.

---

## Try it now

Open the Alexa app on your phone, go to your Shopping List, and add one item right now using the app just to confirm the list is there. Then walk to the nearest Echo speaker and say **"Alexa, add [pick any item] to Grocery List."** Check your phone — it should appear in under five seconds. That is the whole system working. Once it does, your household is ready.
